headline: EBITDA
body:
Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation.

In plain English, it shows how much profit your business makes from its day-to-day trading, before financing decisions, tax and accounting write-downs are taken into account.

Buyers use it because it lets them compare businesses on a like-for-like basis. It is a starting point for valuation, not the whole story.

headline: Adjusted EBITDA
body:
Also called normalised EBITDA.

It is your EBITDA after removing one-off or personal items that will not continue under a new owner. Typical examples are a one-off legal bill, an above-market salary paid to a family member, or a car that is really personal.

These adjustments are called add-backs. Keep a record of them as they happen and your figures will tell a fairer story when the time comes.

5. Is no single customer too large a share?

Three or more yeses is a strong place to start.
